newsitem.title: UK: FedEx crash to cost insurers $115 mln-market.
newsitem.headline: FedEx crash to cost insurers $115 mln-market.

text.p: A Federal Express MD11 cargo aircraft which crashed last night at Newark International airport will be a total constructive loss and cost insurers $115 million, market sources said.
Earlier estimates of around $100 million were given before the crashed MD11 was identified as registration number N611FE, which was built in 1993 and was powered by three General Electric engines.
FedEx's aviation insurance, which is widely spread, is due for renewal tomorrow, said one insurer who is among those providing cover.
Insurance for the aircraft is led out of London by Archer Group, a part of Chartwell Re, market sources said, adding that around 15-20 percent of the risk would be placed in London.
Hours after the crash, firefighters were still battling the burning, charred wreckage with foam.
The airport, one of the busiest in the United States, was closed for several hours before re-opening at 7.33 a.m. EDT (1133 GMT) for some departures.
All five crew escaped with no more than minor injuries after the aircraft crash landed, flipped over and caught fire.
The cause of the accident is not known, but one eye-witness was quoted as saying flames were coming from the MD11 before it crashed.
The accident is likely to be the most costly for aviation insurers so far this year, but is not expected to lead to the rate increases being called for by the industry.
Aviation insurance rates, in common with other classes of insurance, have fallen steadily from a cyclical peak reached in 1992/93.
